newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: SOCCER-GRASSHOPPER LOOKING TO REACH QUARTER-FINALS.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-GRASSHOPPER LOOKING TO REACH QUARTER-FINALS.

text.p: Grasshopper Zurich can all but lock up a place in the quarter-finals of Europe's most prestigious football competition with a victory over French side Auxerre on Wednesday.
Entering the pivotal matches Ajax, Grasshopper and Auxerre are all on six points and Rangers on none, with Ajax leading group A on goal difference.
Playing at home, where they have lost but once this season, Grasshopper will be out to avenge a 1-0 defeat by the French champions two weeks ago.
Based on recent performances, fans at Hardturm Stadium can expect plenty of offensive fireworks.
Grasshopper have won their last three league games in convincing fashion, scoring 13 goals in the process, while Auxerre come into the match off a 7-0 thrashing of Lyon on Friday.
Though they have already scored upset wins over Ajax and Glasgow - the first by any Swiss club in the Champions League - Grasshopper believe they must come away from this match with three points.
Striker Viorel Moldovan, the Swiss league's leading scorer with 14 goals, will lead their attack.
But with the return to form of Swiss international strikers Kubilay Turkyilmaz and Nestor Subiat, the French champions will not be able to concentrate on neutralizing one player.
Grasshopper may have to do without one of their top defenders, Murat Yakin, for the match after he aggravated a knee injury in Saturday's league game.

If he is unable to play, trainer Christian Gross is expected to go with an extra attacker, employing Moldovan, Turkyilmaz and Subiat. The three have proven a lethal combination in league play, combining to score five goals in 30 minutes against Young Boys.

With Yakin out, Grasshopper's bigger problem will be keeping the ball out of their net, a task that will be further complicated by the absence of Alain Geiger, Switzerland's most capped international, who is out with a groin injury.
Auxerre, however, must do without young striker Thomas Deniaud, who scored twice against Rangers and once against Grasshopper in the last two European ties.
He hurt his ankle after scoring the opening goal against Lyon and will be out of action for six weeks.
Coach Guy Roux will also have to juggle his midfield with Ned Zelick, who has a sprained knee, Lilian Laslandes (back spasms) and Sabri Lamouchi (sore knee) missing.
On the positive side for Auxerre, defenders Alain Goma and captain Franck Silvestre have checked out of the infirmary and pronounced themselves fit to play.
"If we lose in Zurich things will become very delicate because we will have to win in Amsterdam," said Auxerre midfielder Christian Henna.

Grasshopper - Pascal Zuberbueler, Brent Haas, Mats Gren, Boris Smiljanic, Pascal Thueler, Massimo Lombardo, Murat Yakin (or Nestor Subiat), Antonio Esposito, Johann Vogel, Kubilay Turkyilmaz, Viorel Moldovan.
Auxerre - Lionel Charbonnier, Alain Goma, Taribo West, Frederic Danjou, Eric Assati, Christian Henna, Philippe Violeau, Moussa Saib, Antoine Sibierski, Steve Marlet, Bernard Diomede.
